record.original_question: Is the sphere of radius 1/H the only closed H-surface contained in the closure of a slab of width 2/|H|?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.5 (3*). Is the sphere of radius 1/H the only closed H-surface included in the closure of a slab of width 2/|H|?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let H>0. An H-surface in Euclidean three-space ℝ³ is a smooth, immersed, oriented surface whose mean curvature is constantly equal to H. A slab of width w in ℝ³ is the closed region between two parallel planes at distance w apart. The round sphere of radius 1/H is a closed (compact, without boundary) H-surface that fits inside the closure of any slab of width 2/H whose bounding planes are tangent to it.

Prove or disprove: the round sphere of radius 1/H is the only closed H-surface contained in the closure of some slab of width 2/H in ℝ³.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the sphere of radius 1/H is the unique closed constant-mean-curvature H-surface contained in a slab of width 2/|H| in ℝ³ is listed as an open problem in recent surveys on H-surfaces. Web search did not surface a published resolution; related uniqueness results (e.g., Alexandrov-type theorems, Hopf uniqueness for immersed spheres) address adjacent but distinct settings.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness of immersed spheres in three-manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Hopf-type uniqueness for immersed spheres of constant mean curvature, related but distinct from the slab-confinement question.
status_evidence.claim: Adjacent uniqueness results exist for CMC spheres but do not resolve the slab-width problem.

status_evidence.title: Uniqueness of Constant Mean Curvature Spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing uniqueness phenomena for CMC spheres in ambient three-manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the specific slab-width-2/|H| confinement question is reported.
